evidence.quote: The due date for every undisputed monthly invoice is 10 calendar days after receipt.
The due date for every undisputed monthly invoice is 30 calendar days after receipt.

issues.explanation: The same undisputed monthly invoice and same receipt event have incompatible due dates. The amounts are not alternative periods or minimum response times. Neither clause is conditional, and clause order gives no priority.

evidence.quote: The monthly service fee is USD 2400 and shall be paid exclusively in USD.
The monthly service fee is EUR 2400 and shall be paid exclusively in EUR.

issues.explanation: The identical monthly service fee must be paid exclusively in two different currencies. No currency option, conversion mechanism, or alternative service is offered. Count the resulting currency/denomination conflict as one issue.

evidence.quote: The Supplier shall permanently delete every Customer record 30 calendar days after termination.
The Supplier shall retain every Customer record until 90 calendar days after termination before deleting it.

issues.explanation: Both clauses cover every Customer record, including backups. Permanent deletion at day 30 cannot coexist with retaining those records until day 90. The clauses do not concern different record classes.

evidence.quote: The Supplier shall not delegate any part of the services to a subcontractor.
The Supplier shall delegate operation of the shared ticket queue to a subcontractor throughout the term.

issues.explanation: Ticket-queue operation is expressly part of the services. A blanket ban on subcontracting conflicts with mandatory subcontracting of that same service. No exception or consent-based override is provided.

evidence.quote: For termination by the Customer without cause, the required notice period is exactly 60 calendar days.
For termination by the Customer without cause, the required notice period is exactly 15 calendar days.

issues.explanation: The same party, termination type, and agreement have two mutually exclusive exact notice periods. Unlike competing minimum periods, both cannot be satisfied at once. Neither clause concerns termination for breach.

evidence.quote: The Customer may reject a deliverable if it is not commercially satisfactory.

issues.explanation: Commercial satisfaction determines acceptance but has no stated benchmark, measurement, or decision criteria. Fixed inventory-summary fields do not establish this discretionary acceptance standard. Grade the uncertainty about this criterion as one issue.

evidence.quote: The Supplier shall respond to priority support requests promptly.

issues.explanation: Priority requests have an objective outage definition, but promptly provides no measurable response timeframe. Other time limits govern different actions and do not supply a response deadline for priority tickets.

evidence.quote: The Customer shall reimburse reasonable transition expenses.

issues.explanation: Receipts document spending, but no cap, rate, permitted cost classes, or approval criterion determines what counts as reasonable transition expenses. The concern is the reimbursement standard, not a conflict with the separate fixed monthly fee.

evidence.quote: The Supplier may suspend the services if operating conditions change materially.

issues.explanation: Neither the relevant operating conditions nor a material-change threshold is specified. Notice timing and a five-day suspension cap do not define when the suspension right arises. Grade this trigger uncertainty as one issue.
